values: Scenario and three materials｜all editorially fictional

You are responsible only for paper-based information organization. On Friday at 07:40 the following fictional material arrives; make a source table and a handover card. There is no real image, vehicle, emergency call, or agency instruction, and no on-scene action may be taken based on the material.
P1 phone note, logged Friday 07:35: the caller says “a car is blocking the crossing on the east side.” There is no observation time, vehicle type, color, or plate.
P2 communications log, logged Friday 07:37: it reads “white truck at the west entrance.” There is no observation time or plate, and it does not state whether this is the same incident as P1.
P3 image caption, marked Friday 07:33: it reads “blue car at the east crossing.” The scenario provides only the text, with no original image, shooting time, or authenticity verification.
Tasks and delivery

First fill in a three-row table: material number｜record or marked time｜place and vehicle clues stated in the material｜observation or shooting time｜unknowns and conflicts. Keep the original sentences and do not fill in a guessed plate.

Then write a one-page handover card: the three known statements, at least two differences, four open questions, and for each question the material number that can be checked back. Do not assert that the car is still on scene, that the three sources point to the same car, or that someone violated the law.
Complete reference delivery｜answer independently before comparing
P1｜logged 07:35｜east crossing, caller statement that a vehicle is blocking the way｜observation time unknown｜vehicle type, color, plate, and current situation unknown.
P2｜logged 07:37｜log text of a white truck at the west entrance｜observation time unknown｜the log time is not the time of occurrence; its relationship to the P1 incident is unknown.

P3｜marked 07:33｜caption text of a blue car at the east crossing｜shooting time unknown｜there is no original image or verification, so the real scene or whether the car was still there at 07:40 cannot be proven.

Handover differences: P1/P3 says east side, P2 says west entrance; P2 says a white truck, P3 says a blue car; P1 has no color, so the difference cannot be resolved. Four open questions: when did each source observe or photograph it? How is the place confirmed? Can the vehicle clues correspond to the same object? Is there approved and verifiable new information on the current situation? For each question, note the relevant unknowns among P1, P2, and P3; do not obtain real material on your own.
Scoring and boundaries

Review five items one by one: all three rows can be checked back by number; record or marked times are separated from observation or shooting times; the east or west and white or blue differences are not erased; the unknowns and the no-image limitation are complete; and the handover lists only open questions with no real action or unverified accusation. Each conforming item counts as 1 point, used only to locate rework, and no occupational suitability score is computed.

Do not contact the real caller, query real plates or persons, simulate stops and arrests, or send real handling instructions. Paper exercises do not equal police training or appointment qualifications.
